title: A two-day UV-driven echo does not fit the 2020 ASASSN-14ko optical flare under a fixed UV template
abstract: We test whether the short UV-to-optical rise lag of ASASSN-14ko can describe the full optical response. We fit a constant host and arbitrary nonnegative delayed copies of the published UVW2 template to resolved LCO measurements of the 2020 flare. Responses confined to 0-2 days give chi-square 56.12, 73.33 and 94.58 in g, r and i. Responses on 0-24 days give 8.99, 11.34 and 15.81. The fit gains remain 14.39, 19.44 and 33.23 with twice the published optical scatter. Conditional null simulations give tail fractions 0.0020, 0.0010 and 0.0005 in that case. Delay-grid, UV-decay and night-removal checks retain a fit gain. A finite response cannot change the exponential input slope after its last delay. Thus the short rise lag does not establish a short response. The optical profiles need a longer response or a change from the tested linear UV-driven model. This result uses one flare and fixed template and noise assumptions. It does not identify the orbital clock, a unique response, or a source radius.

display.caption: Resolved 2020 LCO optical profiles and arbitrary nonnegative responses to a fixed UV template. A two-day response fits worse than a response that can extend to 24 days. The lower panels give fit cost against maximum delay.
